rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so the headroom exists to raise security pressure. This program is a tiny (1977-byte text) numeric benchmark suite with hot loops in fannkuch, spectral-norm, and n-body, so I keep the expensive control-flow passes (BCF, FLA) at moderate runtime/size weights (0.4-0.45) rather than high: they are strong deterrents but would dominate overhead in tight loops, and CorrectnessRisk stays low-moderate since round 0 showed no ICE or miscompile. Cheap, high-yield passes get the strongest security/diversity weights: SUB (arithmetic substitution), IBR (indirect branch rewriting), and SPLIT are near-free transformations well suited to this branch- and arithmetic-dense code, so they will fire broadly across all 8 functions. ICALL and IGV sit in between, adding call-graph and global-variable indirection to break static analysis of the small main/createRandomArray/shuffle cluster without meaningful size cost given the tiny baseline binary. Overall the table biases selection toward low-cost passes applying everywhere while heavier passes apply selectively where function features favor them, maximizing analysis resistance while bounding total runtime and size inflation.
